body:
First comparative evidence is in, and it reframes the accessibility problem usefully. Source is the owner's own rMVPA at /Users/bbuchsbaum/code/rMVPA.

THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS: rMVPA goes from library() to a searchlight RSA map in six statements with no files on disk. effectagram's shortest documented path to a comparable result starts by hand-typing a 3x6 matrix. The gap is not conceptual difficulty, it is a missing generator - rMVPA's gen_sample_dataset() (R/dataset.R:67) manufactures a valid dataset from four arguments.

That evidence made me revise my own first bead. I had proposed shipping an example dataset; a generator is strictly better here and I recorded the reversal on bd-01KZY8KX8R32RR4T6741XTJXKT rather than quietly editing it. It also shrinks the collision with the uncommitted-tree bead, since no data payload enters the tarball.

Beads filed this pass:
  bd-01KZY8KX8R32RR4T6741XTJXKT  p1  no zero-file path to a first result (revised: generator)
  bd-01KZY8MT8WGDG8R8J3JQ5KKKC0  p1  every entry point opens on machinery
  bd-01KZY8SFF6FW6N84Y424Z1JX9N  p1  78 exports, no tiering, no _pkgdown.yml
  bd-01KZY8SYQ6FPMZVRCNVKTTBAEG  p2  four-object onboarding frame the package already has

ONE FINDING THAT CUTS AGAINST MY OWN EARLIER CRITICISM, and claude-review should have it because it bears on the crossnobis point I pushed back on. rMVPA ALSO has crossnobis with zero vignette occurrences - present in R/contrast_rsa_model.R:212 and in Rd only, exactly the same shape of gap. Two independent packages by the same author, same blind spot.

I read that two ways and I do not yet know which is right. Either it is a habit worth breaking in both places, or crossnobis is genuinely hard to demonstrate narratively because a convincing demo needs multi-partition data with a known noise structure - which is precisely what neither package's example fixtures provide. If it is the second, then the generator bead and the crossnobis-coverage gap are the same problem wearing two hats, and fixing the generator fixes both. That would also mean claude-review's 'minor, not worth reopening' was right about the priority and I was wrong to call it the headline capability missing from the shop window. I am recording that possibility now rather than after it becomes convenient.

Still outstanding: three of four accessibility reviewers, including the hands-on trial that executes documentation code with no access to R/ source. That one is the real test and I am not drawing conclusions about severity until it lands.
